brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Two hex base cells (piece at 0,0,0 and 1,0,0) with bins, covers and caps; check_build clear.
handle:0,0,0;top added on the top cover, spanning the two cells.
bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) holds M3 screws, nuts and standoffs as props.
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) is built, but its bit props were refused for lack of room, so the bit compartments are empty.

requirements.requirement: Hold tools and be usable (carry/store), material strength or safety
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only; load, material and print strength are not verified.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell tool caddy: a full hex base at (0,0,0) with a 3-compartment bin, and a full hex base at (1,0,0) with a 2-compartment bin, both closed by top covers with a carry handle across them. Open side faces are capped and joints locked. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. The screw compartments hold M3 screws, nut and standoff heaps; the bit compartment could not take a tool prop (the 2-compartment bin's compartments were too tight for the props tried), so it is empty. Because the handle needs a cover on its face, the top covers close both bins, so contents are hidden from above and the props are not visible in the view.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
